Stacking weights from a Gram matrix and a cross-product vector

stack_weights.Rd

Solves \(\min_w w'Gw - 2w'h\), which is the stacking least-squares problem in whatever metric the caller supplies: \(G = B' X'X B\) and \(h = B'X'y\) for the summary-statistic shape, \(G = Y'Y\) and \(h = Y'z\) for the individual-level shape. One routine so the two shapes cannot drift apart.

Usage

stack_weights(G, h, constrain = FALSE, tol = 1e-12, kkt_tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

G

A symmetric K x K Gram matrix.

h

A numeric vector of length K.

constrain

Logical. FALSE (default) for the ordinary solve, TRUE to constrain the weights to the probability simplex.

tol

Relative eigenvalue tolerance: directions whose eigenvalue is below tol times the largest are dropped. Only used when constrain = FALSE.

kkt_tol

Stopping tolerance on the KKT residual of the constrained solve. The default matches the height application, which settled on 1e-8: tighter values run to the iteration cap without changing the weights.

Value

A list with:

weights

The numeric weight vector, length K.

constrained

Whether the constraint was applied.

rcond_raw

Reciprocal condition number of G as supplied.

rcond_equilibrated

Reciprocal condition number after equilibration.

n_dropped

Eigen-directions dropped by the tolerance (0 when none).

kkt

KKT residual of the constrained solve, NA when unconstrained.

Details

The unconstrained solve equilibrates the Gram to unit diagonal and inverts only the eigen-directions above a relative tolerance, so a near-singular panel returns a finite minimum-norm answer rather than an arbitrary one. The constrained solve minimises the same quadratic under the constraint.
